topPRs.title: feat(op-acceptor): sort tests by previous runtime to front-load longest tests
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds a `RuntimeCache` that persists per-validator wall-clock runtimes to `<log-dir>/runtime-cache.json` between runs
- Before execution, sorts validators longest-first (unknowns sort to the front) so the critical path is front-loaded in parallel mode
- After each run, atomically overwrites the cache with fresh durations
- All failures are soft: a missing, corrupt, or wrong-version cache simply means no sorting optimization — the run is never blocked

## How it works

**Cache format** (`runtime-cache.json`):
```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "updated_at": "2026-02-23T12:00:00Z",
  "runtimes": {
    "TestCheckWithdrawals": "4m20s",
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/op-tests/some/pkg": "8m0s"
  }
}
```

**Execution order:**
1. Unknowns (new tests with no history) — run first
2. Known slow tests — longest first
3. Known fast tests — shortest last

**CI integration** — save/restore `<log-dir>/runtime-cache.json` in your cache config:
```yaml
- restore_cache:
    keys: [op-acceptor-runtime-cache]
- run: op-acceptor --log-dir /tmp/op-acceptor-logs ...
- save_cache:
    key: op-acceptor-runtime-cache
    paths: [/tmp/op-acceptor-logs/runtime-cache.json]
```

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `runner/runtime_cache.go` | New — `RuntimeCache` type, `LoadRuntimeCache`, `SaveRuntimeCache`, `SortWorkByRuntime` |
| `runner/runtime_cache_test.go` | New — 14 unit tests |
| `runner/runner.go` | Add cache fields, load on startup, sort before dispatch, write after run |
| `nat.go` | Pass `RuntimeCachePath` to runner config |

## Test plan

- [ ] All 14 new `TestLoadRuntimeCache*`, `TestSaveRuntimeCache*`, `TestSortWorkByRuntime*` tests pass
- [ ] Full `go test ./...` passes (2 pre-existing timeout test failures unrelated to this change)
- [ ] `go vet ./...` clean
- [ ] Verify CI caches `runtime-cache.json` between runs and subsequent run shows sorted ordering

topPRs.title: feat(op-acceptor): add linux/arm64 release binary
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- Removes the `linux/arm64` ignore entry from `.goreleaser.yaml` so a native linux/arm64 binary is published with each release
- Enables op-acceptor to be pulled and run in a Docker image on Apple M series (arm64) CPUs without emulation
- Also captures logs during test runs to avoid losing output if the process is killed

## Test Plan
- [ ] Verify goreleaser CI produces a `linux/arm64` binary artifact
- [ ] Pull the resulting Docker image on an Apple M-series Mac and confirm op-acceptor runs natively
